description: The ask-a-person main flow's shared vectors (RFC-0014, build plan step 1): the pure half of extensions/ask-person, run by mercury-python and mercury-nodejs against the same file. ticket_cases pin the ticket a payload and a key produce (v1.<payload>.<mac>: the canonical JSON of the payload - keys sorted, no spaces, Unicode kept - and its HMAC-SHA256, both base64url without padding). verify_cases pin how a ticket is read with a list of keys (the current key first, then the previous one) at a given time: the payload, or the exact status and message that refuse it (400 malformed or another version, 403 no key signs it, 410 expired). message_cases pin the message a hold node sends - validated in a fixed order - and the event the channels receive, with requested_at given so the ticket, the link and expires_at are deterministic; or the exact 400 that refuses it. readvice_cases and reply_cases pin the requests the reply page and endpoint send to the engine's entry (the allowlist by graph id, the correlation id header, the turn, the decisions with who decided and when prefixed to each tool call's note; a question's answer unchanged), or the exact refusal. outcome_cases pin what the invoker gets back from the engine's status and body. No HTTP is exchanged by these cases; the transports are tested by each pack against a fake engine. Version 2 (round 4 - the question record): record_cases pin the row a message event becomes in the record (a wait open with its ticket, link and expiry; an advice with none and no state); answer_cases pin the state an answer's outcome leaves (the engine accepted it: answered; nothing was waiting: expired; a refusal or an engine that did not answer: open); transition_cases pin the record's transitions on a scripted sequence - a wait upserted on (graph_id, correlation_id, turn) unless an older message lands late, an advice appended, the first accepted decision standing, the expiry sweep, the change sequence a feed reads from.
